sprint: Active World Reference Lost on Every Reload and Cloud Restore
task: the user rejected the Museum Caption fix as incomplete ('not fixed. you are not able to get to the root of the problem') and supplied a real screen recording of a World-owned 'Cover Titles' text object whose Words field correctly updated after an edit while the canvas stayed frozen on stale content, persisting through deselect/reselect. A faithful in-memory-only reproduction of the exact video scenario passed 10/10, redirecting the investigation toward persistence given the real project's own name, 'Forest Sync - cloud 1.2.' Root cause, confirmed by direct code read: js/projectManager.js's serialize()/deserialize() never saved or restored AppState.project.artworkTheme at all -- a completely separate field from the Story Theme's own AppState.project.theme -- so every World-owned Layer Pack object is resolved through ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme()'s own AppState.project.artworkTheme, and deserialize() only ever called applyTheme(), never applyArtworkTheme(). Two live Playwright reproductions confirmed the real consequence: a genuine page reload + session restore, and js/app.js's checkStudioCloudFreshness() ('Load Cloud Version,' mid-session, no reload at all) both silently lost the active World entirely, vanishing every World-owned object from the render tree and Object Strip. Fixed by adding artworkTheme to serialize()'s payload and restoring + re-applying it via ThemeEngine.applyArtworkTheme(...,{silent:true}) in deserialize(), alongside the existing applyTheme() call -- applyArtworkTheme(null,...) is a safe no-op for a project that never had a World active. Verified via both reproductions re-passing after the fix (render tree and Object Strip correctly show the World-owned objects again, screenshot-confirmed), the original in-memory-only test still passing 10/10 unchanged, and full regression (both goldenBuild.js suites 30/30 each, verify_asset_store_phase_c.js 20/20, verify_phase_e.js 27/27, sync_charm_test.js) passing unchanged. See CLAUDE.md's own entry for the full account, including the honest disclosure that this doesn't perfectly match the video's own frame-by-frame symptom (object vanishes vs. stays frozen) even though it's a real, severe, independently-confirmed defect.
